rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a promising multimodal configuration to establish a baseline. This experiment tests combining scgpt (RNA) and resnet50 (image) with weighted fusion, which balances exploration of key components (modality, encoder types, fusion) while leveraging established models. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines and provides early insights into effective encoder and fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that config_002 (multimodal with resnet50) achieves 52.5% accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) while keeping other settings identical, clarifying whether the image encoder's impact outweighs the current configuration's limitations. This balances exploration of critical components (image encoder) and exploitation of the multimodal framework, which has shown promise.

Existing evidence shows that using ViT-L image encoder (config_022) outperforms resnet50 (config_002). This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer with ViT-L image encoder could further improve accuracy. It explores a promising direction (ViT-L) with a key design choice (aggregation method) that remains untested, balancing exploitation of strong evidence and exploration of critical parameters.

The existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder (config_022) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.542). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from scgpt (used in config_022) to pca_n2000 while keeping ViT and weighted fusion could improve performance. This clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choices with the already promising ViT setup, balancing exploration of key hyperparameters with exploitation of the top-performing image encoder.

The existing evidence shows config_015 (0.635 accuracy) is the best so far using PCA_n2000 RNA, ViT-L image, avgpool, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests replacing weighted fusion with concat fusion using the same RNA and image encoders, which could clarify if fusion method differences impact performance. It directly addresses uncertainty about fusion strategy effectiveness while leveraging the strong RNA/image encoder combination.

The existing evidence shows that using pca_n2000 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_015) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6352). This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation for the same RNA/image encoder pair, which could potentially improve performance by capturing more complex interactions. This clarifies whether transformer aggregation (untested for pca_n2000+imagenet_vit_l) offers gains over avgpool, leveraging the strong foundation of the top-performing RNA/image encoder combination.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using pca_n2000 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders (e.g., config_015) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests a similar setup with scvi_n200 RNA and resnet50 image encoder to compare RNA encoder choices while maintaining avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion. It clarifies whether switching RNA encoders impacts performance, balancing exploration of RNA encoder alternatives with the known strength of imagenet_vit_l for images.

Existing evidence shows config_018 (0.6776 accuracy) is the top performer with scvi_n200 RNA and resnet50 image encoders. This experiment tests switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method unchanged. It clarifies whether transformer aggregation could improve performance for this setup, addressing a key design choice with high potential impact.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_014) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests scvi_n200 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and weighted fusion, exploring whether a different image encoder can further improve performance. It balances exploitation (building on scvi_n200's success) and exploration (testing a new image encoder).

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with singleprofile settings (e.g., config_014) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests a singleprofile setup with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l but uses aggregation None and fusion concat, which could clarify if these parameters are critical. It balances exploration of aggregation/fusion choices while leveraging the proven effectiveness of scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l.
